The LensPin app, step by step

From a camera-photo batch to locations you have checked.

LensPin is not a camera importer or a one-pin editor. It is a native iPhone, iPad, and Mac workflow for camera photos already in Apple Photos: choose the exact batch, build a location timeline, inspect the evidence, and save only approved results.

01 · CHOOSE

Start with the photos you actually want.

Pick a batch directly from Apple Photos or scan a date range. LensPin groups eligible images by camera make and model, then lets you use a GPX track, geotagged iPhone photos, or both.

02 · REVIEW

Triage the whole trip before editing it.

Results are separated into High confidence, Review, and No suggestion. Only strong matches are selected by default; every photo can open into its map, timing, source agreement, and conflict details.

03 · VERIFY

Check the saved photos in Apple Photos.

LensPin rechecks each photo before saving, reports Added, Skipped, and Failed separately, and places successful updates in a LensPin album so the map and coordinates are easy to verify afterward.

Free to start100 successful location additions

Photos and videos share the allowance. Skipped and failed items do not use it. After the free allowance, optional LensPin Unlimited is a one-time purchase (US $3.99 / CN ¥12), not a subscription.

Evidence, not a black box

See why a place was suggested before you save it.

LensPin shows the source, time gap and confidence behind each suggestion. Weak or conflicting evidence is surfaced instead of turned into a guess.

Questions before you start

LensPin FAQ

Do I need a GPX file?

No. LensPin can use geotagged iPhone photos taken around the same time. A GPX track usually gives denser evidence, and you can combine both sources.

Does LensPin import photos from my camera?

No. Import with Apple Photos, a compatible card reader, or the camera maker’s workflow first. LensPin begins after the camera photos are in Apple Photos.

What happens when LensPin is not confident?

The photo moves to Review or No Suggestion with an explanation. Conflicting or low-confidence results are not selected as safe defaults.

Does LensPin change the original capture time?

No. A camera clock offset changes only how LensPin compares the photo with the evidence timeline. The capture time stored with the photo is left alone.

How do I check the locations after saving?

Successful updates are added to the LensPin album. Open a photo there to verify the Apple Photos location, map point, and coordinates.
